# Contract: git-authoring

Third-party skill from [n-shadloo/git-authoring](https://github.com/n-shadloo/git-authoring) (MIT, Nima Shadloo), skills-bundle snapshot 2026-11-13. SumitCraft set the folder name and the description so the skill fills one gap (Commit messages, pull-request text, and everyday git operations). The method is upstream. Category: engineering. Kind: guidance-only (no scripts by design).

## Purpose
Write commit messages, pull-request text, and release notes, and carry out everyday git operations in a repository the user owns.

## Use it for
- "write this commit message"
- "draft the pull request"
- "how do I rebase or undo this commit"

## Not for
- review the diff against a spec (code-review)
- find the commit that broke a test (bisect-anything)

## Accepted inputs
A git repository the user owns, and the change or the question.

## Deliverables
A commit message, pull-request text, release note, or the git operation the user asked for.

## Prerequisites
Required:
- Git

Optional:
- none

Check them with `node tools/doctor.mjs` (Windows: `tools\doctor.ps1`).

## Local and network behaviour
Local git. Opening or merging a pull request needs the user's own GitHub CLI login, and only when they ask.

## Cost-sensitive operations
None.

## Workflow
1. Gather context
2. Understand the change
3. Decide: one commit, or several?
4. Detect the repository's convention
5. Compose the message
6. Self-check
7. Present the exact commit command

Full steps: [SKILL.md](SKILL.md).

## Human decisions
- Whether to push, open, or merge
- Co-author or AI attribution, only if the user asks

## Quality checks
- The message matches the staged diff
- No attribution trailer was added unless requested

## Common failures
- A message written from a guessed diff instead of the staged one

## Limitations
- Guidance. Not run here.
